theme.title: Wilt's impossible season
theme.subtitle: Philadelphia Warriors, 1961–62
theme.recap: Wilt Chamberlain averaged 50.4 points, scored 100 in one night in front of a small crowd and barely left the floor all season.

theme.title: Banner 18
theme.subtitle: Boston, 2023–24
theme.recap: The Celtics led the league by a mile, lost three playoff games and won the franchise's 18th title.

theme.title: Hakeem's Rockets
theme.subtitle: Houston, 1993–95
theme.recap: Houston started 15–0, won a seven-game Finals against New York and then won another title as a sixth seed.

theme.title: Showtime
theme.subtitle: The Lakers of the 1980s
theme.recap: Magic Johnson's Lakers played fast, won big and left Finals marks behind, from a rookie's 42-point clincher to a perfect start to a postseason.

theme.title: Lopsided
theme.subtitle: Blowouts and comebacks
theme.recap: The NBA record book has a 73-point win, a 50-point halftime lead and a 36-point comeback.

theme.title: Russell, Wilt and Baylor
theme.subtitle: The NBA in the 1960s
theme.recap: Boston won eight titles in a row while Wilt, Baylor and West put up numbers that look like misprints today.

theme.title: The 72–10 Bulls
theme.subtitle: Chicago, 1995–96
theme.recap: Chicago lost three games before February, won almost everywhere it played and finished with the best combined record in league history.

theme.title: Heat vs Mavericks, twice
theme.subtitle: 2006 and 2011 Finals
theme.recap: Dwyane Wade carried Miami past Dallas in 2006; five years later Dirk Nowitzki's Mavericks took the rematch.

theme.title: Splash season
theme.subtitle: Golden State, 2015–16
theme.recap: The Warriors won their first 24, reached the All-Star break at 48–4, never lost at home for more than a year and made threes at a rate nobody had seen.

theme.title: Rip City
theme.subtitle: Portland, 1976–77
theme.recap: Bill Walton's Blazers came from 0–2 down to win the 1977 title, then started the next season 50–10.

theme.title: Mamba numbers
theme.subtitle: Kobe Bryant, 1996–2016
theme.recap: Kobe Bryant scored 81 in a night, 62 in three quarters and 40 or more nine games running.

theme.title: Rock bottom
theme.subtitle: The NBA's worst seasons
theme.recap: The 1972–73 Sixers and 2011–12 Bobcats own the worst records ever, and both lost games in long runs.

theme.title: Stockton to Malone
theme.subtitle: Utah Jazz, 1984–2003
theme.recap: John Stockton and Karl Malone played together longer than any teammates, and Stockton barely missed a game.

theme.title: Down 3–1
theme.subtitle: 2016 Finals, Cleveland vs Golden State
theme.recap: Cleveland won the last three games, with LeBron James and Kyrie Irving scoring 41 each in Game 5 and the two teams dead level on points before Game 7.

theme.title: Kareem and the Big O
theme.subtitle: Milwaukee, 1970–71
theme.recap: In only its third season Milwaukee won 66 games and a title behind Lew Alcindor and Oscar Robertson.

theme.title: The Big Three's first year
theme.subtitle: Boston, 2007–08
theme.recap: Boston went from a franchise-worst losing streak to 66 wins and a title won with a 39-point clincher.

theme.title: Clocks, rules and oddities
theme.subtitle: Before and after the shot clock
theme.recap: The shot clock arrived in 1954 after games like a 19–18 final and a six-overtime game with one shot per overtime.

theme.title: Silver and black
theme.subtitle: San Antonio, 1989–2003
theme.recap: David Robinson turned the Spurs around overnight, and Tim Duncan's arrival after a 20-win season started a dynasty.

theme.title: The 1980s Finals
theme.subtitle: Celtics, Lakers and 76ers
theme.recap: Boston and Los Angeles traded titles through the decade, including a Game 5 in a Boston Garden with no air conditioning.

theme.title: Jordan in the Finals
theme.subtitle: Chicago Bulls, 1991–98
theme.recap: Michael Jordan's Finals nights, from 13 straight makes in 1991 to the flu game and the last shot in Utah.

theme.title: Cup nights
theme.subtitle: The In-Season Tournament and NBA Cup
theme.recap: The new in-season event produced its own record nights, plus a prize of half a million dollars a player.

theme.title: Detroit defense
theme.subtitle: Pistons, 1989 and 2004
theme.recap: Detroit won with defense twice: the Bad Boys of 1989 and the 2004 team that held five straight opponents under 70.

theme.title: Triple-double kings
theme.subtitle: Oscar Robertson to Russell Westbrook
theme.recap: Oscar Robertson set the triple-double standard in the 1960s; Russell Westbrook passed his single-season mark in 2017 and his career total in 2021.

theme.title: Shaq and Kobe's three-peat
theme.subtitle: Los Angeles Lakers, 2000–2002
theme.recap: Shaquille O'Neal dominated three straight Finals, and the 2001 Lakers lost just once in the playoffs.

theme.title: Heat wave
theme.subtitle: Miami Heat, 2012–13
theme.recap: Miami won 27 in a row on the way to a second straight title, five years after a 15-win season.

theme.title: The 1970 Finals
theme.subtitle: Knicks vs Lakers
theme.recap: The 1970 Finals had a 60-foot buzzer-beater and Willis Reed's walk-out in Game 7, where Walt Frazier did the damage.

theme.title: Beyond the arc
theme.subtitle: The three-pointer, 1979 to today
theme.recap: It took the NBA years to use the three: the first record was eight in a game and the first 100-three season came in 1988.

theme.title: Houston's high-volume years
theme.subtitle: Rockets, 2007–2019
theme.recap: Houston won 65 games, set a playoff record for missed threes and watched James Harden score 30 night after night.

theme.title: Bird's best Celtics
theme.subtitle: Boston, 1985–86
theme.recap: Larry Bird won a third straight MVP, Boston lost once at home all season and the Celtics beat Houston for the title.

theme.title: Warriors vs Cavaliers
theme.subtitle: The 2015 and 2017 Finals
theme.recap: Golden State won the first and third of four straight Finals meetings, with both sides setting records along the way.

theme.title: Philadelphia's juggernauts
theme.subtitle: 76ers, 1966–67 and 1982–83
theme.recap: Philadelphia built two of the most dominant teams ever: Wilt's 68-win champions and the 1983 team that nearly swept the playoffs.

theme.title: Miller time
theme.subtitle: Reggie Miller's Pacers
theme.recap: Reggie Miller tormented the Knicks, made threes in 68 straight games and once scored eight points in under nine seconds.

theme.title: Lakers lore
theme.subtitle: Minneapolis and Los Angeles
theme.recap: Long before Showtime the Lakers had Elgin Baylor's Finals record and a 1971–72 team that did not lose for two months.

theme.title: Crowds, ratings and parades
theme.subtitle: Who was watching
theme.recap: From 4,000 people in Hershey to 108,713 in Texas, the NBA's audience numbers swing wildly.

theme.title: The beautiful game
theme.subtitle: San Antonio, 2013–14
theme.recap: The Spurs passed Miami off the floor in the 2014 Finals, a year after losing to them, with a record ten international players.

theme.title: Seventies Finals
theme.subtitle: The NBA, 1975–79
theme.recap: The late 1970s spread titles around: Golden State swept, Boston won a triple-overtime classic and Seattle won its first title.

theme.title: Warriors from deep
theme.subtitle: Golden State shooting records
theme.recap: Golden State's shooters broke records for threes in a game, threes in a playoff game and threes in consecutive games.

theme.title: The Worm
theme.subtitle: Dennis Rodman
theme.recap: Dennis Rodman, a second-round pick, won seven straight rebounding titles and grabbed rebounds at a rate not seen since Wilt.

theme.title: One year apart
theme.subtitle: The 2008 and 2009 Finals
theme.recap: The Lakers lost a 21-point first-quarter lead to Boston in 2008, then came back to win the 2009 title.

theme.title: Swat team
theme.subtitle: Blocked-shot records
theme.recap: Blocks were first counted in 1973–74, and the records include Elmore Smith's 11 in a half and Dwight Howard's nine in a Finals game.

theme.title: The dynasty years
theme.subtitle: Chicago Bulls, 1991–98
theme.recap: Chicago won 69 games a year after 72, buried Utah by 42 in a Finals game and then fell to 13 wins once the team broke up.

theme.title: Golden State's fourth
theme.subtitle: The 2022 Finals
theme.recap: The Warriors won a fourth title in eight years behind Stephen Curry and a 21–0 run in the clincher.

theme.title: Playoff drama
theme.subtitle: 2002 to 2005
theme.recap: Boston shot its way past Philadelphia and erased a big deficit against New Jersey, and Robert Horry stole a Finals game in Detroit.

theme.title: Bubble and beyond
theme.subtitle: The 2020 and 2021 Finals
theme.recap: The Lakers won in the 2020 bubble; a year later Giannis Antetokounmpo scored 50 to finish Phoenix.

theme.title: Shortened seasons
theme.subtitle: Lockouts and the pandemic
theme.recap: The NBA has cut its schedule to 50 games, 66 games and 72 games, and the shortened years still produced champions.

theme.title: Scoring outbursts
theme.subtitle: Big nights
theme.recap: Wilt owns most of the scoring records, but Devin Booker and Kobe Bryant added 60-plus nights at both ends of a career.

theme.title: Lakers–Celtics, 2010
theme.subtitle: The 2010 Finals
theme.recap: The rivalry's latest Finals went seven games, with Ray Allen setting a record one night and missing everything two nights later.

theme.title: The 2020s
theme.subtitle: Recent records
theme.recap: A 41st pick won Finals MVP, an eighth seed reached the Finals and a rebuilding Spurs team lost 18 in a row.

theme.title: Warriors, Cavs and Raptors
theme.subtitle: The 2018 and 2019 Finals
theme.recap: LeBron James scored 51 in a 2018 loss; a year later Toronto ended Golden State's run.

theme.title: Miami's Finals years
theme.subtitle: Heat, 2012 and 2013
theme.recap: Miami beat Oklahoma City and then survived San Antonio, thanks in part to a corner three with seconds left.

theme.title: Going to work
theme.subtitle: Detroit Pistons, 2003–04
theme.recap: Detroit's defense-first underdogs rallied after a midseason trade and toppled a star-studded Lakers team for the title.

theme.title: Mile High first
theme.subtitle: Denver Nuggets, 2022–23
theme.recap: Behind Jokić, Murray and a deep supporting cast, Denver earned the top Western seed and won the NBA championship for the first time.

theme.title: The Answer's run
theme.subtitle: Philadelphia, 2000–01
theme.recap: An MVP guard, a midseason defensive anchor and two Game 7 battles took Philadelphia all the way to a hard-fought Finals.

theme.title: The Cow Palace sweep
theme.subtitle: Golden State, 1974–75
theme.recap: The Warriors defeated the favored Bullets by winning close games behind Rick Barry, a deep bench and a relentless second-half defense.

theme.title: Twin Towers rise
theme.subtitle: San Antonio Spurs, 1998–99
theme.recap: The Spurs overcame a difficult lockout-season start and rode Duncan and Robinson to the franchise's first championship.

theme.title: The youngest MVP
theme.subtitle: Chicago Bulls, 2010–11
theme.recap: Derrick Rose led Chicago to the NBA's best regular-season record before the Bulls' deep playoff run ended against Miami.

theme.title: Seven Seconds or Less
theme.subtitle: Phoenix Suns, 2004–05
theme.recap: Steve Nash returned to Phoenix, Mike D'Antoni unleashed a rapid-fire attack, and the Suns transformed into the league's most electric regular-season team.

theme.title: We the North
theme.subtitle: Toronto Raptors, 2018–19
theme.recap: Kawhi Leonard arrived, the Raptors survived a Game 7 buzzer-beater and then won Canada's first NBA championship.

theme.title: The ATL uprising
theme.subtitle: Atlanta Hawks, 2014–15
theme.recap: A balanced Atlanta team went unbeaten in January, won a franchise-record 60 games and claimed the East's top seed.
